clue.text: Sit once more in tranquillity

definitions.meaning: to pose again, read as RE- plus POSE, sitting for a portrait a second time

explanation.surface: Someone sits down again and finds peace.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits the answer as RE-POSE: to pose, or sit for an artist, again.
explanation.definitionFit: Repose is a state of rest and calm, a close synonym for tranquillity.

clue.text: Study absorbing info about English traitor

indicators.note: the study word takes another piece into its middle, swallowing it

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the info word is read backwards

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A scholar researches the background of an English turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the info word and 'absorbing' puts it inside the study word; gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A renegade deserts a cause or side, which is what a traitor does.

clue.text: Alleviate pressure on my total earlier food intake

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
all means the whole amount, a total
the speaker's word for themselves, I
ate is the past tense of eat, food taken in earlier

explanation.surface: A dieter hopes to ease the strain on their calorie count from earlier meals.
explanation.definitionFit: To palliate is to ease pain or symptoms without curing, the same as to alleviate them.

clue.text: Rising stars around independent channel

indicators.note: the reversed stars go around the next piece, enclosing it
in a down clue rising means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: suns are stars

explanation.surface: New celebrities appear on an independent TV station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' turns SUNS into SNUS; 'around' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy a sinus is a cavity or narrow passage, so a channel in the body.

clue.text: Palace player going too far in a large undergarment

indicators.note: the actor sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large
a bra is an undergarment
a ham is an actor who overacts

explanation.surface: A hammy performer overdoes it while wearing an oversized bra.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alhambra is the Moorish palace and fortress complex in Granada, Spain.

clue.text: Liberals seem upset by society's work on injustice

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: Liberal politicians are distressed by a social campaign against injustice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the two words, leaving the society S to finish the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Victor Hugo's novel Les Misérables is a famous book about poverty and unfair punishment.

clue.text: Do I take drug, on turning up to get some protein?

parts.note: the question 'Do I take...?' is recast as 'Am I...?'

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the little word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: acid is slang for LSD

explanation.surface: A worried person asks whether they have taken drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks 'Am I on acid?', but 'turning up' flips ON to NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Amino acids are the building blocks that link up to form proteins, so one is part of a protein.

clue.text: Canadian songster scoffing a trifle

indicators.note: to scoff is to eat greedily, so the singer swallows the next piece

parts.note: Michael Bublé is a Canadian crooner

explanation.surface: A Canadian crooner gobbles up a sponge pudding.
explanation.walkthrough: A trifle is also a British layered dessert of sponge, custard and cream, which the surface pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A bauble is a showy trinket of little value, so a trifle in that sense.

clue.text: See 18
News about cycle of regularly fabricated material

indicators.note: the news letters go about, surrounding the picked letters

parts.note: N for new, doubled as plurals of abbreviations often are, gives two Ns for news

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words cycle of

explanation.surface: A news story covers the regular cycle of manufacture of a material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes YLO from 'cycle of' (second, fourth and sixth letters); 'about' puts them between two Ns.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic polymer fabric, a material made in a factory.

clue.text: Boss losing face in dog-tired state

indicators.note: the shortened boss word goes inside the dog

parts.note: Lassie is the famous collie of film and television

indicators.note: losing face means dropping its first letter

parts.note: a boss is a stud, a raised knob or ornament

explanation.surface: An embarrassed boss collapses, dog-tired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing face' cuts STUD to TUD, and 'in' puts it into LASSIE. 'dog-tired' looks like one word, but 'dog' is the collie.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassitude is physical or mental weariness, a state of being tired.

clue.text: Scandal involving royal house making bit of capital

indicators.note: a -gate scandal named for what it involves, so the scandal word is tacked on after the house

parts.note: Lancaster was an English royal house in the Wars of the Roses
-gate is the suffix for scandals, after Watergate

explanation.surface: A scandal at the palace is a gift to the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: Lancaster Gate is an area and Tube station in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster Gate is a district of London, so a part of the capital city.

clue.text: Slides, as with sliding rocks

indicators.note: rocks means shakes about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A landslide description: slides happen as rocks slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' rearranges AS and SLIDING together.
explanation.definitionFit: In music glissandi are continuous glides from one pitch to another, slides on an instrument.

clue.text: Pirouetting priest in party is slippery

indicators.note: spinning round, so the whole is read backwards
the priest goes inside the party

parts.note: a do is a party
Eli is the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: A clergyman spins on the dance floor at a party and is slippery underfoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the priest inside the party, giving DELIO; 'Pirouetting' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something oiled has been greased, so it is slippery.

clue.text: Business that's going to set up partnerships?

definitions.text: Business that's going to set up partnerships?

parts.words: Business that's going to set up partnerships?
parts.note: sounds like a firm forming commercial partnerships, but 'going' is going out, and the partnerships are romantic

explanation.surface: A firm planning to form business partnerships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going' hints at going out together, which is what this business arranges.
explanation.definitionFit: An agency that matches people for romance sets up couples, a kind of partnership.

clue.text: What makes middle of cell right after fresh clean out

indicators.note: the right letter comes after the rearranged ones
fresh means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Scientists clean out a laboratory before a fresh experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges CLEAN OUT into NUCLEATO, and R follows.
explanation.definitionFit: The nucleus is the core of a cell, and a nucleator is something that starts a nucleus forming.

clue.text: Cleric rejected papers cutting about sex

indicators.note: the papers cut into the sex word

parts.note: carnal means relating to sexual desire

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the papers are read backwards

parts.note: ID is identity papers

explanation.surface: A churchman tosses aside the newspapers that cut into stories about sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' reverses the papers and 'cutting' places them in the sex word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal is a senior Catholic churchman, a member of the College that elects the pope.

clue.text: Praise dropping a train network for non-union shenanigans

indicators.note: dropping means one letter is let go from the praise word

parts.note: to adulate is to praise excessively
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Rail bosses stop praising the train network during a dispute with non-union workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' takes an A out of ADULATE to leave ADULTE. 'Non-union' looks like a trade-union matter but means outside marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Adultery is sexual misbehaviour outside the marriage union, playfully called shenanigans.

clue.text: The Met Office?

parts.note: the Met Office is Britain's weather service, but the Met is also London's Metropolitan Police, whose headquarters is meant

explanation.surface: Britain's national weather forecasting service.
explanation.walkthrough: The Met Office is the UK's weather service; the Met here is the Metropolitan Police of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Scotland Yard is the London headquarters of the Metropolitan Police, so it is the Met's office.

clue.text: Feature of Copenhagen — Danish design kept secret

definitions.meaning: a cryptic sense: the words Copenhagen and Danish have a plan word concealed across them, which is their feature
a plan or motive that is not disclosed

explanation.surface: A notable thing about Copenhagen is its Danish design.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: AGENDA sits concealed across copenHAGEN DAnish, so a concealed agenda is literally a feature of those words. Danish design, the famous furniture style, misdirects.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden agenda is a secret plan or motive, and a design is a plan.

clue.text: Olivier periodically dressed in check cloth

indicators.note: the picked letters are dressed in, clothed by, the check word

parts.note: to vet is to check

indicators.note: periodically means taking letters at regular intervals, here the even ones

explanation.surface: Laurence Olivier sometimes wore a checked suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'periodically' takes the even letters of Olivier, and 'dressed in' wraps the check word round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Velvet is a soft fabric with a dense pile, a type of cloth.

clue.text: Divine Greek female and Frenchman on island

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the island

parts.note: René is a French man's name

explanation.surface: A Greek goddess and a Frenchman share an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Irene was the Greek goddess of peace, a deity and female.

clue.text: Person to copy European-style bread sandwiches

indicators.note: the bread holds the other pieces between its parts

parts.note: a roll is bread
mode is a style or fashion

explanation.surface: A Continental-style loaf is used for sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like a noun, but it is the verb putting two pieces inside the bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A role model is someone whose behaviour others imitate, a person to copy.

clue.text: For example, stupid flipping sucker!

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: dim means stupid

explanation.surface: Someone curses a fool as a stupid flipping sucker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' is a mild British oath in the surface but turns EGDIM round.
explanation.definitionFit: A midge is a tiny biting insect that sucks blood, so it is a sucker.

clue.text: Time off saved duty at work

indicators.note: at work means the letters are working, set in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone saved up their duty hours while at work.
explanation.walkthrough: A duvet day is a British workplace term for a day off taken when you just want to stay in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Duvet days are days of unscheduled leave from work, which is time off.

clue.text: Versifier performed in recital

indicators.note: a recital is spoken out, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: something performed is done

explanation.surface: A poet performs at a recital.
explanation.definitionFit: John Donne was a metaphysical poet, and a versifier is a writer of verse.

clue.text: Legal authorities excluding one sign

parts.note: not means leaving out, as in 'everyone, not him'
Aries is one sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Lawyers exclude a single signature from a document.
explanation.definitionFit: Notaries are officials licensed to certify documents, legal authorities.

clue.text: A second tie put on where actors perform

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means the put word comes after

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre, where a company of actors performs
to lay something is to put it down

explanation.surface: A second play is put on at the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: A tie is a British cup match; a drawn one is played again.
explanation.definitionFit: A replay is a match played again after a draw, so a second tie.
